column1: # Cebuano object focus (stage 6, tunatale-ve4p.32). Hand-written; NOT checked by a native speaker.
# root<TAB>English<TAB>English past<TAB>mo-<TAB>mi-<TAB>-on<TAB>gi-<TAB>objects (noun=its English when it is not the one meant; ...)
# Each row makes four sentences per doer, one per cell (focus_sentences.focus_sentence):
#   Moinom ko og tubig.   I'll drink water.        actor focus, not begun
#   Miinom ko og tubig.   I drank water.           actor focus, begun
#   Imnon ko ang tubig.   I'll drink the water.    object focus, not begun
#   Giinom ko ang tubig.  I drank the water.       object focus, begun
# Wolff, under -un_1: "Palitun ku ang bábuy, I will buy the pig. Gipalit ku ang bábuy, I bought the pig."
# Checked 2026-10-15 against Wolff, A Dictionary of Cebuano Visayan (1972; Gutenberg #40074). Every root
# is class a, which takes the direct passive: inum [A; a2] drink · káun [A2S3S; a] eat · dala [A; a2]
# take, bring, carry · tan-aw [A; ab2] see, look at. Every form is counted in native news as spelled
# (cebuano_focus_counts.tsv for -on and gi-, cebuano_affix_counts.tsv.gz for mo- and mi-).
# The -on column is written down because spell() cannot make it: imnon, kan-on (Wolff kan-un) and dad-on
# (Wolff dad-un, also dalhun) drop or change a vowel. kan-on is also the noun "cooked rice", so it is
# never an object of kaon.
# Left out: hulat (its actor forms are mag-/nag- only), luto (lutoon 8, lutuon 13), sulat (sulaton 2),
# lakaw and adto (motion: no object to focus).
# tan-aw is "look at", not the "watch" of its mo-mi row: the owner's nouns are a house and a vehicle.
inom
kaon
